note: Explicit allow-list for capstone->keystone semantic round-trip. Each entry is a literal 'orig => new' pattern with the reason it is not a semantic change. Anything not listed here is a defect; there is no catch-all rule.

entries.pattern: add byte ptr ds:[rax], al => add byte ptr [rax], al
entries.why: default ds: segment override is implicit; keystone prints the operand without it

entries.pattern: mov r11, qword ptr gs:[0x10] => mov r11, qword ptr gs:[rip + 0x10]
entries.why: keystone re-encodes a gs:[disp] operand as rip-relative and drops the segment override; operand value preserved, presentation differs

entries.pattern: mov rax, qword ptr gs:[0x30] => movabs rax, qword ptr gs:[0x30]
entries.why: capstone names the 64-bit absolute form movabs where the source was a segment-relative mov; same instruction, alias only

entries.pattern: sal byte ptr [rax], 1 => shl byte ptr [rax], 1
entries.why: sal and shl share the same opcode (d0/d1); capstone prints sal for shl 1
sysret and sysretq are the same opcode, presented with a REX.W suffix
